rows.title: The six hours after chest pain: what actually decides the outcome
rows.heading: The Six Hours After Chest Pain: What Decides The Outcome
rows.excerpt: Heart muscle does not wait. Here is what happens between the first symptom and the cath lab — and the part of it you control.
rows.body:
Heart muscle starts dying within minutes of a blocked artery. Everything that happens in the next six hours is a race against that clock — and a surprising amount of it is decided before anyone reaches a hospital.

The first thirty minutes

Most delay is not in the ambulance. It is at home, in the gap between "this does not feel right" and picking up the phone. The average patient in our district waits just over ninety minutes before calling for help.

If chest pain lasts more than fifteen minutes, do not drive yourself. Call.

What we do while you travel

An ECG is taken within ten minutes of arrival, troponin is run at the bedside, and the cath lab team is paged before the report finishes printing.
